title: Draw the bottom bar out of a small pile while holding the bars it carries
instruction: Draw the red bar out endwise from under the two crossing bars and lay it on the yellow pad. Do not let any of the other four bars move more than 1 cm or turn more than 5 degrees while you do it.
context: Material movers and stock handlers often need one length of stock from the bottom of a pile whose upper layers are too long or too heavy to lift off and restack. Pulled on its own, the bottom piece drags the load resting on it off the pile, so one hand holds the load still while the other draws the piece out.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. All bars are loose, planed pine, with their edges square to the table. Bottom row, three bars lying side by side on the table, long side left to right, 2 mm apart: two plain bars, each 30 mm (front to back) x 260 mm (left to right) x 30 mm tall, 120 g, centred 26.8 cm and 33.2 cm in front of the arm bases on the midline (each spans 13.0 cm left to 13.0 cm right of the midline); and between them the red bar (painted red), 30 x 320 mm and 34 mm tall, 160 g, centred 30.0 cm in front of the arm bases, its right end flush with the plain bars' right ends (13.0 cm right of the midline) and its left end 6.0 cm beyond theirs (19.0 cm left of the midline). The red bar is 4 mm taller than the plain bars, so it alone carries the layer above. Top layer, two crossing bars, each 120 mm (front to back) x 30 mm (left to right) x 30 mm tall, 55 g, lying across the red bar with their long side front to back, centred 30.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 1.6 cm left and 1.6 cm right of the midline (2 mm apart), their undersides on the red bar's top, 34 mm above the table and 4 mm above the plain bars' tops; each spans 24.0 to 36.0 cm in front of the arm bases, over all three bottom bars. Yellow pad (fixed, yellow plastic sheet taped to the table): 70 mm (front to back) x 360 mm (left to right) x 2 mm, centred 17.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 32.0 cm left of the midline (spanning 13.5 to 20.5 cm in front and 14.0 to 50.0 cm left). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The protected bars are the two plain bars and the two crossing bars. A protected bar is disturbed if, at any moment of the trial, its centre has moved more than 10 mm (in any direction) from where it started, or it has turned more than 5 degrees from its starting orientation; this is judged over the whole trial, as a person watching the video would, and putting a bar back afterwards does not undo it. At rest means moving less than 1 cm/s and turning less than 0.5 rad/s. A bar rests on a surface when its underside is within 1 mm of it. The layer is down when both crossing bars rest on the two plain bars (undersides 29 to 31 mm above the table) and are at rest, and the plain bars are at rest. The red bar is lying flat when its top is at most 40 mm above its underside (34 mm as it started, 30 mm on its side; standing on end or propped up at one end does not count). Score 1.0: no protected bar disturbed, the layer down, and the red bar at rest, lying flat and resting on the pad (underside 2 to 3 mm above the table), with its footprint inside the pad's edges (1 mm allowed). Score 0.5: no protected bar disturbed, the layer down, and the red bar at rest, lying flat and resting on the table or partly on the pad, with no part of its footprint over the pile's footprint (the rectangle covered by the three bottom bars at the start: 25.3 to 34.7 cm in front of the arm bases, 13.0 cm left to 13.0 cm right of the midline). Score 0.25: the same, except that the red bar is still partly inside the pile's footprint, with its right end more than 3.1 cm left of the midline (past the crossing bars, so they no longer rest on it). Score 0 in every other case: the red bar still under the crossing bars, held above the table or pad by more than 1 mm, standing on end, lying on another bar or still moving; the crossing bars held more than 1 mm above the plain bars; or any protected bar disturbed at any time, whatever happens afterwards. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the condition at the last step.
reset_notes: Lay the three bottom bars back side by side, 2 mm apart, with the red bar in the middle and its extra 60 mm to the left; lay the two crossing bars back across the red bar, 2 mm apart, centred on the midline. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. Every bar is a rigid box with the simulator's rubber-like friction for loose objects (static 1.2, dynamic 1.0), higher than dry wood on wood. Masses assume pine at about 500 kg/m3. The 4 mm extra thickness of the red bar, which puts the whole top layer on it, is the simplification that makes the hold necessary: in a real pile the load is shared unevenly in ways that are hard to reproduce. The pad is a fixed 2 mm plate.
